keyECGEvidence: Sinusoidal amplitude modulation with axis twisting
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Electrolyte-induced Long QT Syndrome (LQT) secondary to gastrointestinal losses and medication-induced prolongation
modelResponse.mechanism: Prolonged repolarization (QTc 618 ms) due to hypokalemia (K 2.9 mmol/L LOW), hypomagnesemia (Mg 1.2 mg/dL LOW), and hypocalcemia (Ca 7.9 mg/dL LOW) exacerbated by additive QT-prolonging drugs (Sotalol, Azithromycin, Ondansetron) leading to early afterdepolarizations and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

rejectedAlternatives.why: Morphology shows axis twisting/amplitude modulation characteristic of Torsades rather than a fixed axis.
The rhythm shows a discernible, albeit twisting, sinusoidal pattern rather than completely disorganized electrical activity.

recommendedActions: Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate (e.g., 2g over 1-2 mins) per ACLS/Torsades protocol
Aggressive electrolyte replacement (Potassium and Magnesium) to target high-normal levels
Initiate IV fluid resuscitation for hypotension and dehydration
Prepare for synchronized cardioversion or defibrillation if patient becomes pulseless or hemodynamically unstable
